requirements.text: The replacement catalytic converter, as a separate technical unit, shall be type-approved as a pollution control device for fitting to M1 vehicles as a replacement part.
The replacement catalytic converter shall be designed, constructed and capable of being mounted so that the vehicle complies with the Regulations it originally complied with.
The replacement catalytic converter shall enable pollutant emissions to be effectively limited throughout the normal life of the vehicle under normal conditions of use.
The replacement catalytic converter shall be designed to be installed at the exact position of the original pollution control device.
Where the original converter has oxygen probes and other sensors, the replacement catalytic converter shall keep their exhaust-line position unmodified.
Where the original equipment converter includes thermal protections, the replacement catalytic converter shall include equivalent protections.
The replacement catalytic converter shall be designed, constructed and mounted to obtain reasonable resistance to corrosion and oxidation under the vehicle's conditions of use.
The M1 vehicle equipped with the replacement catalytic converter shall be subjected to a type I test per the annexes of Regulation No. 83 to compare performance with the original converter.
The test vehicle with a new original converter shall be run in with 12 extra urban cycles (type I, part 2) to establish the comparison basis.
After preconditioning, the test vehicle shall be conditioned in a room held at a temperature between 293 K and 303 K (20 °C and 30 °C).
The conditioning shall last at least six hours and continue until the engine oil and coolant temperatures are within ±2 K of the room temperature.
Three type I exhaust gas tests shall subsequently be made with the original converter to determine the basis for comparison.
The original converter of the test vehicle shall be replaced by the replacement catalytic converter submitted for test.
The replacement catalytic converter shall be run in with 12 extra urban cycles (type I test part 2) before the emission tests.
The replacement catalytic converter conditioning shall last at least six hours and continue until the oil and coolant temperatures are within ±2 K of room temperature.
Three type I exhaust gas tests shall be made with the replacement catalytic converter.
The test vehicle with the original converter shall comply with the type-approval limit values, including the deterioration factors applied at the vehicle type approval.
The mean value M of the emissions with the replacement catalytic converter shall satisfy M ≤ 0.85S + 0.4G for each regulated pollutant.
The mean value M of the emissions with the replacement catalytic converter shall not exceed the limit value G for each regulated pollutant.
The emissions evaluated for the replacement catalytic converter shall be the regulated pollutants CO, HC, NOx, particulates and particles, or the sum HC + NOx.
The reference value S shall be the mean of the three type I test emissions obtained with the original converter.
The limit value G shall be the type-approval emission limit divided by the multiplicative or minus the additive deterioration factors.

Where the replacement catalytic converter is fitted to a vehicle approved to the 06 series of amendments to Regulation No. 83, the regulated pollutants shall be all pollutants of paragraph 5.3.1.4. of that series.
The replacement catalytic converter shall satisfy the technical requirements of Regulation No. 59 regarding noise and vehicle performance.
The maximum absorbed power measured on a chassis dynamometer with the replacement catalytic converter shall not be lower by more than 5 per cent than with the original equipment converter.
The replacement catalytic converter shall comply with the durability requirements of paragraph 5.3.6. of Regulation No. 83, i.e. type V test or the deterioration factors of the table.
For a positive-ignition engined M1 vehicle, the deterioration factors applied shall be 1.2 for CO, 1.2 for HC, 1.2 for NOx and 1.2 for HC+NOx.
Where the original converter was monitored in the original configuration, the replacement catalytic converter shall demonstrate OBD compatibility.
The compatibility of the replacement catalytic converter with the OBD system shall be demonstrated using the procedures of Annex 11, Appendix 1 to Regulation No. 83.
Prior to installation of the replacement catalytic converter the OBD system shall indicate no malfunction and store no fault codes.
The malfunction indicator shall not activate during the vehicle operation required by paragraph 5.2.2. with the replacement catalytic converter fitted.
The replacement catalytic converter conforming to an approved type shall bear an international approval mark affixed conspicuously in the place specified on the approval form.
The approval mark on the replacement catalytic converter shall comprise a circle surrounding the letter E followed by the distinguishing number of the granting country.
The approval mark shall show the number of this Regulation, the letter R, a dash and the approval number in the vicinity of the circle.
The approval mark shall be indelible and clearly legible when the replacement catalytic converter is mounted under the vehicle.
The approval mark applied to the replacement catalytic converter shall have a minimum dimension a of 8 mm.
Each new replacement catalytic converter shall be indelibly marked with the manufacturer's name or trade mark.
The replacement catalytic converter shall be accompanied by information on the vehicles, including year of manufacture, for which it is approved.
Where applicable, the information shall include a marking identifying whether the replacement catalytic converter is suitable for fitting to an OBD-equipped vehicle.
Where necessary, the replacement catalytic converter shall be accompanied by installation instructions.
The required information shall be provided as a leaflet accompanying the replacement catalytic converter, or on its packaging, or by any other applicable means.
The sample of the replacement catalytic converter submitted shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the applicant's trade name or mark and its commercial designation.
Where the replacement converter is a periodically regenerating system, the emission, noise, durability and OBD requirements of paragraphs 5.2.3., 5.3., 5.4. and 5.5. shall apply.
The replacement catalytic converter shall be qualified for the M1 vehicle category covered by this Regulation.
The replacement catalytic converter shall ensure that tailpipe emissions are effectively limited throughout the lifetime of the vehicle under the specified test conditions.
Where a type 3 test is performed on the vehicle fitted with the replacement converter, the crankcase ventilation system shall not permit crankcase gases to reach the atmosphere.
Where the type 6 low-temperature test is performed, the carbon monoxide and hydrocarbon emissions of the vehicle shall be below the limits of Table 2.
For an M1 vehicle of category M, the type 6 low-temperature limits shall be 15 g/km of CO and 1.8 g/km of HC.
Where the type 6 test is performed, the ambient test temperature shall be 266 K (-7 °C).
For each pollutant, at least two of the three type 6 test results shall be below the limit.
One of the three type 6 test results may exceed the limit, but by no more than 10 per cent.
The vehicle shall be deemed satisfactory in the type 3 test if, in every measurement condition, the crankcase pressure does not exceed the prevailing atmospheric pressure.
During the type 3 test, the intake manifold pressure shall be measured to within ±1 kPa.
During the type 3 test, the vehicle speed indicated at the dynamometer shall be measured to within ±2 km/h.
During the type 3 test, the crankcase pressure shall be measured to within ±0.01 kPa.
The type 3 measurements shall be performed at idling and at 50 km/h ±2 in the third gear or drive position.
During the type 6 test the ambient temperature shall average 266 K ±3 K and stay between 260 K and 272 K.
During the type 6 test the ambient temperature shall not fall below 263 K or exceed 269 K for more than three consecutive minutes.
The fuel used for the type 6 test shall comply with the reference fuel specifications of Annex 10, paragraph 2.
Before the type 6 driving schedule begins, the test cell temperature measured in the cooling fan air stream shall be 266 K ±2 K.
Before the type 6 test, the vehicle shall be stored for at least 12 hours and not more than 36 hours under the standard soak method.
The type 6 sampling shall begin before or at engine start and end after the final idling period of the last elementary cycle, after 780 seconds.
During the type 6 test the vehicle heating and defrosting devices shall be shut off.
For an M1 vehicle approved to Euro 7A, the emission character in the approval mark shall be FL.
The approval mark affixed to the vehicle shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The approval mark shall be placed close to or on the vehicle data plate.
Where in-service conformity of the vehicle fitted with the replacement converter is checked, it shall be done between 15,000 km or 6 months and 200,000 km or 10 years, whichever occurs sooner.
Where the vehicle is in the additional lifetime, a durability multiplier of 1.2 shall be applied to adjust the gaseous pollutant emission limits.
The manufacturer shall perform in-service conformity testing for tailpipe emissions comprising at least the type 1 test for all ISC families.
For the type 1 in-service conformity statistical procedure, the minimum sample size for a pass shall be three vehicles and the maximum cumulative sample size ten vehicles.
An in-service conformity emissions test shall be considered passed for a pollutant when its result is equal to or below the applicable emission limit of UN Regulation No. 154.
The pollution control systems installed together with the replacement converter shall minimise vulnerabilities that may lead to tampering to the fullest extent possible.
The pollution control system shall be protected against unauthorised modification of engine or sensor control unit data or software code.
The pollution control system shall prevent unauthorised alteration of emission-related signals by physical modifications.
Where the type 3 test is required, it shall be carried out on the positive-ignition vehicle after it has been subjected to the type 1 test.
Within ten minutes of completing the type 6 preconditioning, the engine shall be switched off.
The type 6 test fuel shall be at a temperature no higher than 289 K (+16 °C) when filled.
When analysing the type 6 exhaust samples, care shall be taken to prevent condensation of water vapour in the sampling bags.
Where the first type 6 result for each pollutant is less than or equal to 0.70 L, only one test shall be performed.

The replacement catalytic converter, where it is an electrical/electronic sub-assembly, shall comply with the electromagnetic compatibility requirements applicable to components fitted in M1 vehicles.

The electrical/electronic systems associated with the replacement catalytic converter shall be designed, constructed and fitted so that the vehicle complies with this Regulation in normal conditions of use.
Where the replacement catalytic converter includes an ESA, that ESA shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions and for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
The broadband radiated emissions of the ESA shall stay below 62 to 52 dBµV/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band and 52 to 63 dBµV/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band.
The broadband radiated emissions of the ESA shall stay below a constant 63 dBµV/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
The measured broadband emission values of the ESA, in dBµV/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
The narrowband radiated emissions of the ESA shall stay below 52 to 42 dBµV/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band and 42 to 53 dBµV/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band.
The measured narrowband emission value of the ESA, in dBµV/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
For an ESA on a 12 V system, the maximum allowed transient conducted disturbance on the supply lines shall be +75 V for positive polarity and -100 V for negative polarity.
The ESA immunity test level over 90 per cent of the 20 MHz to 2 GHz band shall be 60 V/m for stripline, 75 V/m for TEM cell, 60 mA for BCI, 30 V/m for ALSE and 21 V/m for reverberation chamber.
The minimum ESA immunity test level over the whole 20 MHz to 2 GHz band shall be 50 V/m for stripline, 62.5 V/m for TEM cell, 50 mA for BCI, 25 V/m for ALSE and 18 V/m for reverberation chamber.
The ESA shall comply with the immunity requirements if no degradation of performance of immunity related functions occurs during the Annex 9 tests.
For transient pulse 1 immunity, an ESA on a 12 V system shall withstand -75 V for 500 pulses with functional status III.
For transient pulse 2a immunity, an ESA on a 12 V system shall withstand +37 V for 500 pulses with functional status I for immunity related functions.
For transient pulse 3a immunity, an ESA on a 12 V system shall withstand -112 V for 1 hour with functional status I for immunity related functions.
For transient pulse 3b immunity, an ESA on a 12 V system shall withstand +75 V for 1 hour with functional status I for immunity related functions.
Where the ESA does not include an electronic oscillator operating above 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with the narrowband emission limits of paragraph 6.6.2.
The ESA of the replacement catalytic converter conforming to an approved type shall bear the approval mark described in paragraph 5.3.
The ESA approval mark shall comprise a circle containing the letter E followed by the distinguishing number of the granting country.
The ESA approval mark shall show the number of this Regulation, the letter R, a dash and the approval number to the right of the circle.
The ESA approval mark need not be visible when the ESA is installed in the vehicle.
The approval mark affixed to the ESA shall have a minimum dimension a of 6 mm.
The ESA sample submitted shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark and the type designation.
Where a component sold as aftermarket equipment is not related to immunity related functions, no type approval is needed provided a manufacturer's declaration of conformity is issued.
Where vehicle broadband emissions are measured at 10 m, the limits shall be 32 dBµV/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band and 32 to 43 dBµV/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band.
Where vehicle broadband emissions are measured at 10 m, the limit in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band shall remain constant at 43 dBµV/m.
Where vehicle narrowband emissions are measured at 10 m, the limits shall be 28 dBµV/m in the 30 to 230 MHz band and 35 dBµV/m in the 230 to 1,000 MHz band.
The vehicle immunity field strength shall be 30 V/m over 90 per cent of the 20 MHz to 2 GHz band and at least 25 V/m over the whole band.
Where BCI testing is used, the current shall be 60 mA over 90 per cent of the 20 MHz to 2 GHz band and at least 50 mA over the whole band.
The vehicle shall comply with the immunity requirements if no degradation of immunity related functions occurs during the Annex 6 tests.
The vehicle radiated emission limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for ALSE or outdoor test site measurements.
Where peak detectors are used for the vehicle emission measurements, a correction factor of 20 dB shall be applied.
The vehicle shall be exposed to electromagnetic radiation in the 20 to 6,000 MHz range in vertical polarization during the immunity test.
The immunity test signal shall use AM modulation with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth in the 20 to 400 MHz range.
During the 50 km/h immunity mode, a speed variation greater than ±10 per cent of the nominal speed shall constitute a failure.
During the 50 km/h immunity mode, a complete stop of the front wiper shall constitute a failure.
During the vehicle immunity test, the engine shall turn the driving wheels at a steady speed of 50 km/h unless a different condition is technically justified.
For the ESA broadband emission measurement, the extraneous noise or signal shall be at least 6 dB below the limits of paragraph 6.5.2.1.
Where peak detectors are used for ESA emission measurements, a correction factor of 20 dB shall be applied.
For the ESA narrowband emission measurement, the extraneous noise or signal shall be at least 6 dB below the limits of paragraph 6.6.2.1.
ESA narrowband emission measurements shall be performed with an average detector.
ESA immunity measurements shall be made in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range with frequency steps according to ISO 11452-1.
The ESA under test shall be switched on and stimulated to be in its normal operating condition during the immunity tests.
For conformity of production, the measured vehicle emission levels shall not exceed the reference limits by more than 4 dB (60 per cent).
For conformity of production of an ESA, the measured emission levels shall not exceed the reference limits of paragraphs 6.5.2.1. or 6.6.2.1. by more than 4 dB.
For conformity of production, the vehicle shall show no degradation of direct-control functions when subjected to 80 per cent of the immunity reference field strength.
Where the ESA is powered by low voltage, a 5 µH / 50 Ω artificial network shall be used for the emission and immunity measurements.
The artificial network shall be mounted directly on the ground plane and its grounding connection bonded to the ground plane.
Before testing, a test plan shall be prepared containing at least the mode of operation, stimulated functions, monitored functions, pass/fail criteria and intended emissions.
Where the ESA shall be operational during engine start phases, it shall withstand the starting profile at test level II for 10 pulses.
The vehicle fitted with the replacement catalytic converter shall meet the emission limits set out in UN Regulation No. 83.
Where the replacement converter is a periodically regenerating system, the original system of the test vehicle shall be replaced by it for the emission test.
The replacement catalytic converter shall be designed to also meet the emission requirements introduced by the 09 series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 83, as applicable.
Where the vehicle's low-temperature range ratio is verified, the check shall pass if the reported ratio multiplied by 1.04 is at least equal to the declared ratio.
